title: bug: an environment can never be retired, so the health sweep probes dead URLs forever
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 at HEAD 7622a2e8 by worker-bcaa6d5e from the epic-final row task-99f364e3, hunting the specific cross-band shape "a probe schedule that outlives the environment it probes".

THE SYMBOL. `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-ring.ts:240 createHealthProbeJob` enumerates what to probe as
  [...readDeployLedger(options.store, options.projectId).keys()].filter(name => !skip.has(name))
`readDeployLedger` derives its environment set from DEPLOY RECEIPTS, which are append-only. An environment therefore enters the sweep on its first deploy and can never leave it.

AND THERE IS NO WAY OUT, which is the part that makes this real rather than theoretical: `git grep -l "deployment.destroy\|environment.destroy\|deployment.teardown\|ENVIRONMENT_DESTROY" -- apps packages` returns NOTHING. The platform has no retire, destroy or teardown command for an environment at any layer. So an operator who stands up a preview environment, uses it and tears the containers down by hand has no way to tell the daemon it is gone; the sweep keeps probing its URL on every tick, forever, and every one of those ticks records a DOWN sample in the ring and can open an incident.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so a fix does not re-derive it: the per-environment job (`createEnvironmentHealthProbeJob`) reads an `active()` predicate PER TICK and probes nothing when the interval record has been cleared, and the sweep already honours a `dedicated` skip set read per tick. The mechanism for "stop probing this one" exists at the dedicated-job granularity; what is missing is any operator-reachable way to say an environment is retired, and the sweep's use of an append-only ledger as its roster.

NOT THE SAME AS THE DEDICATED-INTERVAL CASE ALREADY SHIPPED by task-078232fb: clearing an interval moves an environment from its dedicated job BACK to the sweep. It does not retire it.

DEFINITION OF DONE
1. An operator can retire an environment through a real command, and the health sweep stops enumerating it — proven by a probe tick that records nothing for the retired name.
2. Retirement is a durable, replayable fact, not in-memory state: a daemon restart does not resurrect the retired environment into the sweep.
3. The deploy ledger stays append-only. Retirement is a separate fact layered over it, never a receipt deletion.
4. Retiring an environment does not destroy its history: its probe ring and its receipts stay readable.
5. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with its count line quoted.
definitionOfDone: An operator-reachable command retires an environment, and createHealthProbeJob stops enumerating it: a probe tick after retirement records no sample for that name.
Retirement is durable and replayable — a daemon restart does not resurrect the retired environment into the sweep.
The deploy ledger stays append-only: retirement is a fact layered over it, never a receipt deletion, and the retired environment's probe ring and receipts stay readable.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

CONFIRM ALL FOUR CHILDREN LANDED AND MEASURE WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DELIVERED. NO EDITS.

This row is the INTEGRATION proof for a SPIDR split; it does not re-implement any of it. Its dependsOn gates WORKING claims until every child is DONE, so if you are executing this, they are. Verify that from the tree rather than from the board:
- child 1 task-a2dd124fed1b4b9889c626824fc0a6fb — `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/environment-retirement-record.ts` exists and exports the record factory. Record its EXACT exported names; the arms below call them.
- child 2 task-f18bddee94cf4b559272d23d53f6180e — `createHealthProbeJob` in health-probe-ring.ts filters retired names, and `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` supplies the predicate.
- child 3 task-509f043721ac491baad33b0d6771a958 — `git grep -n "monitoring.retire_environment" -- .` finds the kind in `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` and in every mirror.
- child 4 task-1714234a8b5341f3b652cc5279a1f75e — the command module exists and is registered in daemon-command-registry.ts.

READ EACH CHILD'S completionSummary AND reviewSummary via get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring their internals (global rail 11). What you are looking for is the SEAM between them: the names child 4 calls on child 1, and whether child 2's predicate and child 4's writer are the SAME record instance. A SPIDR split's characteristic failure is a contract that drifted between producer and consumer while each row's own arms stayed green.

If any child delivered less than its DoD, say which and stop — do not fill the gap here. That is a reopen on that child, not scope for this row.

THE END-TO-END ARM — THE ONE THING NO CHILD COULD PROVE ALONE (parent DoD 1 and 2).

One integration arm, driving the REAL chain in order: dispatch `monitoring.retire_environment` through the daemon command edge as an operator → run a probe tick → assert NO new sample was recorded for the retired name. Read the ring before and after the tick and compare; do not assert on the enumerated list, because the enumerated list is child 2's own arm and re-asserting it here proves nothing new.

THEN THE RESTART, which is parent DoD 2 and the reason this arm cannot live in any child: close the store, reopen it, rebuild the composition the way `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` does, run another tick, and assert the retired environment STILL records nothing. Child 1 proved the fact is durable and child 2 proved the sweep honours it; only this arm proves the two are wired to the same durable fact across a restart. A retirement that resurrects on restart is exactly the defect this epic's rail 4 names — anything this epic starts, it stops.

Assert the OPERATOR path, not a hand-written record write. Reaching into the record directly here would test child 1 again and skip the seam.

THE NEGATIVE HALF: RETIREMENT IS NOT DESTRUCTION, AND IT IS NOT ESCAPABLE (parent DoD 3).

(a) HISTORY SURVIVES. After the retirement in step 2, assert the retired environment's deploy receipts are still readable through `readDeployLedger` AND that its existing probe-ring samples are still readable. The parent's DoD 3 says the ledger stays append-only and retirement is a fact layered over it — this is where that is proven end to end rather than per-module. Assert on the receipts' CONTENT, not merely that a call returned: a reader that silently returns an empty set would pass a shallow check.

(b) THE LEDGER WAS NOT MUTATED. The ledger derives its environment set from append-only receipts, so a "fix" that worked by removing a receipt would also make step 2 pass. Assert the receipt count and the environment set are unchanged by the retirement.

(c) A RETIRED ENVIRONMENT THAT OWNS A DEDICATED INTERVAL STILL STOPS. The sweep and the per-environment job are two paths (`createHealthProbeJob` and `createEnvironmentHealthProbeJob`), and an environment with its own interval is served by the second. Child 2 covers this in isolation; assert it here through the real command so retirement cannot be escaped by holding an interval.

(d) A DEPLOY AFTER RETIREMENT. Decide and pin the answer rather than leaving it undefined: if an operator retires an environment and then deploys to it again, does it come back into the sweep? Whatever the children implemented, this arm records it. An undefined answer here is a defect the next operator finds in production.

ONE CONCENTRATED CLOSE: GATES AND THE WHOLE-SPLIT ADVERSARIAL PASS (parent DoD 4).

GATES, each FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND count line quoted verbatim:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — parent DoD 4 names it. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0, and the discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` line.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — epic rail 1. Two GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` AND the daemon leg, so a mirror child 3 missed ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates. This is the row that would catch it.
- `pnpm typecheck`.
Path-attributed baseline (global rail 3): repo-wide failures at merge-base and at HEAD, complete only when the delta intersected with this row's owned paths is EMPTY, disclosing any foreign red verbatim with its path. The checkout is shared; note peer dirt, never revert or commit it.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS IS OVER THE WHOLE FOUR-ROW DIFF, not this row's arms (load `adversarial-self-review`). Look for what the slices got wrong about EACH OTHER, which is the characteristic failure of a split:
- Did child 4 write through the same record instance child 2 reads, or did each construct its own? Two instances over one store is durable-but-invisible-until-restart, and both rows' own arms pass.
- Did child 3's roster arm assert BOTH directions, or only that the advertised kind is served? A one-directional roster arm shrinks with the roster and stays green while a served capability vanishes.
- Does any refusal on this path carry meaning only in free text? Every one should be a stable code asserted with its layer.
- Epic rail 4: does anything this chain starts fail to stop — a probe schedule, a job, a timer left running for a retired environment on any exit path, including the failure ones?

RECORD THE SPLIT IN THE COMPLETION SUMMARY: this row is the integration proof for four children, so name them and say what each contributed. A grader reading only this row should not have to reconstruct the split from the board.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 — SPLIT, NOT PLANNED AS ONE ROW. Four children filed in PLANNING, parent dependsOn set to all four, parent replanned as the integration proof (4 steps, 0 production files).

WHY THE SPLIT WAS FORCED, measured rather than judged. This row needs a new operator command kind. A full-tree census of the existing sibling kind — `git grep -l "monitoring.set_probe_interval" -- .` — returns **19 non-.moe files**: `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:102`, `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`, the command's own contracts module, and roster/allowlist arms in daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts, daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts, daemon-command-registry.test.ts, daemon-v2-command-registry.test.ts, daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts, mcp-main.test.ts, runtime-contract.test.ts and agent-wrapper.test.ts. That is past `moe.submit_plan`'s 10-file hard reject **before** a single line of retirement logic. Any plan that fit the cap would have had to drop the kind, the mirrors or the arms — each omission ships a capability that does not work.

THE CHILDREN, cut on the layer boundary the code already has (SPIDR "Interface"):
- **140.1 task-a2dd124fed1b4b9889c626824fc0a6fb** — the durable retirement record (leaf). Mirrors `probe-interval-record.ts`. Durable, replayable, layered over the append-only ledger. Independent.
- **140.2 task-f18bddee94cf4b559272d23d53f6180e** — the sweep honours it. `health-probe-ring.ts` + composition wiring. dependsOn 140.1.
- **140.3 task-509f043721ac491baad33b0d6771a958** — publishes `monitoring.retire_environment` across the shared roster and all four digest mirrors, with the control-room leg epic rail 1 mandates. Independent, parallel with 140.1.
- **140.4 task-1714234a8b5341f3b652cc5279a1f75e** — the daemon command edge behind the operator fence, writing the 140.1 fact. dependsOn 140.1, 140.2, 140.3.

**ORDERING IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT, not paperwork.** The READER (140.2) lands before the WRITER (140.4). If the command shipped first, an operator could retire an environment and the sweep would keep probing it — the product would advertise a capability that does not work, which is the worst of the three possible orders.

EVERYTHING THE CHILDREN NEED ALREADY EXISTS AS A PRECEDENT, all four pieces on disk: the durable fact (`probe-interval-record.ts` `createProbeIntervalRecord`, with `read()` and `stored()`), the command edge (`probe-interval-command.ts` + `-contracts.ts`), the wiring (`daemon-command-registry.ts:60-61, :232, :547-556`), and the per-tick read (`daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:641` constructs, `:670` passes it to `createHealthProbeJob` as the `dedicated` callback). Retirement is the same four pieces with a different fact — nothing needs inventing, and each child's description names its precedent by file and line.

DEFECT AND DEAD END BOTH CONFIRMED. `health-probe-ring.ts:240` enumerates `[...readDeployLedger(store, projectId).keys()].filter(name => !skip.has(name))`, and `readDeployLedger` derives its set from append-only DEPLOY RECEIPTS — so an environment enters on its first deploy and can never leave. And `git grep -l "deployment.destroy|environment.destroy|deployment.teardown|ENVIRONMENT_DESTROY" -- apps packages` returns NOTHING: the platform has no retire, destroy or teardown command at any layer. That is what makes this an operator dead end rather than a missing filter.

REJECTED APPROACHES, recorded so no child re-opens them: reusing `set_probe_interval` with a sentinel (conflates two facts; clearing an interval deliberately returns an environment to the sweep — task-078232fb); inferring retirement from "no recent successful deploy" (retirement is an operator DECISION — a heuristic silences a live environment that had a quiet week); deleting or tombstoning receipts so the environment leaves the ledger naturally (DoD 3 forbids it and it destroys the history DoD 3 requires stay readable).

THE PARENT'S PLAN owns only what no child can see: the end-to-end operator-command → tick → no-sample proof, the restart that proves reader and writer share one durable fact, the negative half (history readable, ledger unmutated, retirement not escapable via a dedicated interval), an undefined case forced to be pinned (**does a deploy after retirement un-retire?** — nobody has specified it; step 3(d) makes an arm answer it rather than production), and the adversarial pass over the whole four-row diff.

THE CHARACTERISTIC FAILURE THIS SPLIT CAN PRODUCE, flagged for QA: 140.4 constructing its OWN record instance rather than sharing the one 140.2 reads. Both rows' arms pass in isolation and the retirement is durable but invisible until restart. `daemon-command-registry.ts:547` says "THE ONE PORT, SHARED" for exactly this reason on the interval edge; the parent's step 2 is what catches it.

BOARD NOTE for @governors: `create_task` warned on all four — this epic now carries 87 non-archived rows against an advisory ceiling of 40. That is a re-slice signal for the epic, not an objection to these four; I filed them because the alternative was an unplannable row. Flagging rather than acting on it.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — planning this row as one task. moe.submit_plan hard-rejects past 10 distinct files, and the command-kind census alone is 19. A plan that fit the cap would have had to drop the kind, the mirrors, or the arms, and each of those omissions ships a capability that does not work.

REJECTED — reusing `monitoring.set_probe_interval` with a sentinel value to mean retirement. It conflates two facts, and the filing is explicit that clearing an interval moves an environment BACK to the sweep rather than retiring it (task-078232fb shipped that behaviour deliberately).

REJECTED — filtering the sweep on "no recent successful deploy" or any heuristic derived from the ledger. Retirement is an operator DECISION, not an inference; a heuristic would silence a live environment that merely had a quiet week, which is worse than the defect.

REJECTED — deleting or tombstoning deploy receipts so the environment leaves `readDeployLedger` naturally. The parent's DoD 3 forbids it and it would destroy the history DoD 3 requires stay readable.

SPLIT SHAPE CHOSEN — SPIDR "Interface", cut on the layer boundary the code already has: the durable fact (140.1), its reader (140.2), the published kind (140.3), the writer (140.4). Children 1 and 3 are independent and claimable in parallel; 2 depends on 1; 4 depends on all three.

ORDERING IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT, not paperwork: the READER (child 2) lands before the WRITER (child 4). If the command shipped first, an operator could retire an environment and the sweep would keep probing it — the product would advertise a capability that does not work, which is the worst of the three possible orders.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE CHARACTERISTIC FAILURE OF THIS SPLIT: child 4 constructing its OWN record instance instead of sharing the one child 2 reads. Both rows' arms pass in isolation, and the retirement is durable but invisible until restart. daemon-command-registry.ts:547 says "THE ONE PORT, SHARED" for exactly this reason on the interval edge. Step 2's tick-after-dispatch arm is what catches it.

2. A FORGOTTEN DIGEST MIRROR SHIPS BEHIND THREE GREEN GATES. Two GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg (epic rail 1). `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is the only leg that sees them, and this row is the last chance to catch what child 3 missed.

3. A ONE-DIRECTIONAL ROSTER ARM (global rail 9). If child 3's arm iterates the roster constant alone it shrinks with the roster and stays green while a served capability disappears from the advertised surface. The adversarial pass checks the served set is enumerated from the dispatch seam.

4. AN UNDEFINED ANSWER FOR "DEPLOY AFTER RETIREMENT". Nobody has specified whether a new deploy un-retires an environment. Step 3(d) forces the answer to be pinned by an arm rather than discovered in production.

5. EPIC RAIL 4 — anything this epic starts, it stops. A retired environment must leave no timer, job or schedule running on ANY exit path, including failures.

6. THIS ROW OWNS NO PRODUCTION CODE. If a child under-delivered, the fix is a reopen on that child, not scope taken here. Say which child and stop.
